channel.description: Latest articles from Otago Daily Times (odt.co.nz)

item.title: Djokovic outlasts Sinner to set up Alcaraz final
item.description: An exhausted Novak Djokovic after defeating Jannick Sinner in five sets in Melbourne. Photo: Reuters Novak Djokovic turned back the clock to dethrone Jannik Sinner in a five-set classic and set up a final showdown with world number one Carlos Alcaraz after the Spaniard slogged through the longest Australian Open semi-final against Alexander Zverev.

item.title: Witness describes 'desperate' scenes following fatal crash
item.description: Flowers left at the base of a power pole that was replaced after being struck in the crash. Photo: Gregor Richardson A witness to last night's fatal crash in Port Chalmers says residents had noticed the vehicle being driven recklessly in the area before it smashed into a power pole.

item.title: Catherine O'Hara, star of 'Schitt's Creek' and 'Home Alone', dies
item.description: Catherine O'Hara at the 2019 Critics Choice Awards. Photo: Reuters Catherine O’Hara, the shape‑shifting Canadian comic actor whose characters ranged from the deliriously theatrical Moira Rose in "Schitt's Creek" to the frantic mother in “Home Alone,” has died at 71 — prompting an outpouring of tributes led by her co-star Macaulay Culkin and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.

item.title: One in five schools scrutinised by ERO needs support or intervention
item.description: ERO is unable to tell RNZ if it's making more recommendations for support or intervention in schools than in the past. Photo: Getty Images By John Gerritsen of RNZ

item.title: More than 200 killed in mine collapse
item.description: Laborers dig at the Rubaya coltan mine, in the town of Rubaya, which is controlled by M23 rebels, in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in March last year. File photo: Reuters More than 200 people were killed this week in a collapse at the Rubaya coltan mine in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Lubumba Kambere Muyisa, spokesperson for the rebel-appointed governor of the province where the mine is located, told Reuters on Friday.

item.title: More than 3 million pages of Epstein files released
item.description: A redacted image released by the Justice Department showing some of Epstein's allies and accomplices. Photo: US Department of Justice The US Justice Department on Friday published millions of new files related to the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, including emails that show Howard Lutnick, President Donald Trump's commerce secretary, apparently visited Epstein's private island for lunch years after he claimed to have cut off ties.

item.title: Community pays tribute to 'true Southern girl'
item.description: Jillian Clark. Photo: supplied A Milton veterinarian who died in a suspected homicide has been remembered as "the perfect example of a beautiful human" by her friends and family.

item.title: Mount Maunganui landslide: Rotorua grandmother's remains identified
item.description: Rotorua woman Susan Knowles has been formally identified as a victim of the Mt Maunganui landslide. Photo: Supplied The remains of Rotorua property manager Susan Knowles have been formally identified by the coroner.

item.title: More than 40 rescued before tourist boat capsizes
item.description: Chris Friedman and girlfriend Alona, after the boat they were on sank in Akaroa. Photo: Chris Friedman A passenger aboard a tourist boat that ran aground outside Akaroa Heads on Banks Peninsula on Saturday says some on board were panicked and crying, when they realised the vessel was in trouble.
